summary: Muskegon South Breakwater Light: a red steel pyramidal tower at the end of the arrowhead pier, built 1929-1931 for the outer light of a range; unmanned, now viewable from outside only.

structures.note: 63 ft (19 m) overall: a 10 ft rectangular base and a 53 ft pyramidal tower (virtual tour). Build year given as 1929, 1930 or 1931 by different sources

access.note: Viewable from the exterior only (Muskegon Lights). Not open for visits inside; severely deteriorated.

facts.agency: U.S. Coast Guard maintains the aids to navigation; Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy holds possession of the tower since 2010

events.note: Construction begins on the arrowhead harbor; the breakwater light is at its outer end
Temporary light established 1929 (Muskegon Lights history); the 1929 works summary lists the light and fog-signal station in progress that year
Steel pyramidal tower and fog horn completed in 1930 (Muskegon Lights history). The virtual tour gives 1931
Virtual tour gives 1931 as the year the tower was built; NRHP significant year 1931
Listed on the National Register of Historic Places (NRIS 06001026)
Declared excess property by the U.S. Government
Possession awarded to the Michigan Lighthouse Conservancy under the National Historic Lighthouse Preservation Act

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Work began 1927; the Bulletin's 1929 summary lists the station in progress that year; the Muskegon Lights history says a temporary light was established in 1929 and the steel tower and fog horn were completed in 1930. first_lit is set to 1929, the temporary light. The virtual tour and the NRHP significant year give 1931; the 1930 completion and the 1931 date are kept as conflicts.
The record's 'active' status is consistent with the Coast Guard still operating the light (Muskegon Lights home page).

notes_for_editor: Thin station: no keepers are recorded for this light (USLHS place record lists 'Minor Aid to Navigation' with no people; the virtual tour says the structure was not meant to be manned). No storms, wrecks or rescues are tied to this light in the sources used. The Muskegon South Pierhead roster (USLHS, 28 lines) belongs to the pierhead station, a different record (us-mi-muskegon-south-pierhead), and is not used. Build year conflicts: 1929 (temporary light), 1930 (completed, Muskegon Lights history; the record's first_lit), 1931 (virtual tour and NRHP significant year); unresolved. Wikipedia was consulted for leads only and not cited: it gives a 1928 caisson, a 1929 superstructure, 1939 equipment, 'in service since 1879', and a 1934 grounding of the SS Henry Cort off the breakwater; none of these is sourced here. One Chronicling America search for the Henry Cort grounding (1934) returned unrelated Muskegon-matching pages; not used. The 1928 Bulletin mentions a partial wrecking of the fog-signal house 'at Muskegon' in the 8 December gale; the Bulletin does not say which Muskegon station, so it is not used. The NRHP nomination (06001026) is not digitised (22 KB placeholder). The LighthouseFriends page for this light was not located; its pierhead page (ID 191) is used only for the earlier lights. The record's access ('unknown') could be updated to 'exterior only' per the Muskegon Lights home page; this is a status note, not a correction. The record's characteristic (Iso R 6s) and focal height were not re-verified.
